reply.rationale: No defensible compositional paradigm survives the evidence test. The two-character codes (TA, BO, CE, WC, etc.) look like mnemonic labels for whole procedures, but there is no stable substitution frame with recurring parts whose meanings compose predictably across multiple entries. Shared initials/finals are not semantically consistent: e.g. C appears in C, CE, CT, CA, CW with unrelated contributions; T appears in T, TA, CT, RT with incompatible roles; L in LB cannot be justified as the standalone L 'left'. The digit symbols 1–14 also behave as opaque indexed procedures rather than literal counts. Standalone symbols such as G/M/Fm and T/B/L/K may suggest semantic families, but without attested multi-morpheme contrasts in a shared frame they do not license classes or segmented entries. Therefore the safest analysis is a flat lexicon.
